title: Flattened event store for Console cost & feature usage attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a flattened event store and supporting ETL that produces denormalized daily and hourly fact tables for Console feature usage and per-route cost attribution. This ticket covers schema design, transformation logic, incremental materialization, partitioning strategy, and backward-compatible migration from current canonical route/event tables. Goal: enable fast analytics queries for product, billing, and cost ops teams without expensive joins across multiple curated tables.
acceptance_criteria: Daily and hourly flattened_day_events and flattened_hour_events tables exist in the analytics dataset
Tables include canonical keys (workspace_id, route_id, user_id, session_id), derived feature flags, token_cost_estimate, and routing_tier attributes
ETL supports idempotent incremental updates using event watermark and SCD2 for route metadata
Query performance: common 30-day cost-attribution query runs under 60s on preview infra
Migration plan documented and backward compatible with existing dashboards; no consumer breakage
tasks: Finalize schema and column definitions with product and billing owners
Implement Spark/DBT transformation with streaming micro-batch ingestion hook
Add partitioning by ds and hour and clustering on workspace_id, route_id
Set up CI tests and row-level lineage assertions
Run backfill for last 90 days and validate counts against canonical tables
Publish confluence spec and link dashboards to new tables
Coordinate rollout with Console backend owners and data consumers

notes: Design decisions: denormalized store chosen to optimize common cost and product queries; primary trade-off is storage overhead vs query latency
Backfill strategy: use windowed processing with dedupe by (event_id) and watermark of 7 days to avoid late-arrival reprocessing
Monitoring: add row-count drift alert and weekly lineage table comparisons to detect regressions
Rollout plan: 1) staging backfill and validation, 2) canary workspace subset (20 workspaces), 3) full prod swap with read-through fallback for 2 weeks
